Definition: from G1097; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.):--advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will.
BiblicalUsage: gnṓmē means advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will. In Acts 20:3, the text says "he purposed to return through Macedonia." In 1 Corinthians 1:10, the text says "but [that] ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment."
TheologicalSignificance: What gnṓmē teaches me is that wisdom begins with fearing the Lord, and it shows in how we live, not just what we know. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
